title: The Choir of the Weeping Wood Anew
premise: Coral Brightwater, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things until he discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies. The prophecy names him as both the war's spark and its only extinguisher: his hidden bloodline carries the true name of the Weeping Wood, and speaking it aloud would either free the enslaved forest-spirits or reignite the ancient war that burned the world once before. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and shadowed by a guildmate who loves him but serves the usurper, Coral must choose between loyalty to the guild that raised him and the truth the ledgers have always concealed. In the end, Coral speaks the name at the heart of the Weeping Wood — not to wage war, but to unbind it — sacrificing his swordspeech and his memories of the woman he loves, while she chooses to remember for both of them.
about_author: Ansel Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts in coastal libraries, an obsession that bleeds into every ledger-bound corner of their fiction. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things that should never have been written down.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Coral Brightwater catalogs the night's impossible trades — bottled thunder, a borrowed shadow — in the Guild's undercroft, establishing his meticulous voice and quiet loneliness. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: contentment laced with restlessness; Coral senses something is missing from a life built on other people's wonders.

chapters.title: A Date Written Before Tonight
chapters.summary: Auditing the prophecy vault, Coral finds today's exact date inked a century ago, describing 'the last swordspeaker opening the sealed page.' The page after it is fused shut. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm as the ledger he trusts turns against him.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kind Lie
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vess orders Coral to seal the vault and forget it, revealing she has known about the prophecy for years. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty; Coral obeys, but begins copying records in secret.

chapters.title: Sera of the Ninth Stair
chapters.summary: Sera Quill, Coral's closest friend among the guild archivists, catches him forging an entry and covers for him without asking why. Their easy intimacy deepens into something unspoken. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: warmth and guilt; Sera realizes she would break rules for him, a dangerous admission.

chapters.title: What the Swordspeaker Swore
chapters.summary: Coral performs a routine swordspeaking — commanding a bound blade with spoken oaths — and feels the magic falter, as if something is listening. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: unease turning to wonder; his power responds to the prophecy's pull.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Auditors
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halven Marr arrives from the capital demanding all prophecy holdings, wearing the guild's own stolen seal. Vess stalls; Coral hides the fused book inside a trade-goods crate. POV: Halven. Emotional beat: predatory patience; Halven suspects the last swordspeaker still lives.

chapters.title: The Fused Page Opens
chapters.summary: Blood from a paper cut — Coral's blood — unseals the second page, which describes this very hour: 'the swordspeaker flees through the weeping trees.' Outside, the Wood itself begins to move. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: vertigo; prophecy stops being text and becomes weather.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: Pursued by Halven's soldiers, Coral flees into the forest where trees bleed sap like tears and whisper fragments of his childhood. The Wood knows him. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: terror braided with belonging; the forest feels more like home than the guild ever did.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Deep in the Wood, Coral meets Wren Ashvale, a spirit-warden who greets him by a name he has never heard — his true one. She claims they loved each other in a life he cannot recall. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: aching recognition; love arriving as memory rather than discovery.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Burned Century
chapters.summary: Wren shows Coral the Wood's own record: living rings that archive the ancient war, when swordspeakers enslaved the spirits and were cursed in turn. His order was not noble; it was penance. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: faith shaken; every oath he has sworn was written by the guilty.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: In the city, Sera trades guild secrets to Halven — feeding him false ones — to buy time for Coral, binding herself to a man she despises. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: self-loathing courage; loyalty expressed as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Name in the Roots
chapters.summary: Wren teaches Coral that his blood holds the Wood's true name: speaking it frees the spirits or arms them for war, depending on the heart of the speaker. He practices and nearly loses himself. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: temptation; power offering everything at the price of becoming a weapon.

chapters.title: Halven at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Halven's armies reach the Wood's edge, burning the outer groves. The trees' screams are audible for miles. POV: Halven. Emotional beat: cold triumph curdling; the burning Wood answers back, and Halven feels watched.

chapters.title: Vess Comes Alone
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Vess walks unarmed into the Wood, confessing she is Coral's mother and helped hide him as an infant — and that she wrote part of the forged history he trusted. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: shame and fierce love; truth offered too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Face
chapters.summary: Halven reveals Sera's bargain to her, then breaks it, using her access to locate the Wood's heart. Sera escapes with the one map that matters. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: devastation into resolve; she stops protecting herself and starts protecting Coral.

chapters.title: Armies of Sap and Ash
chapters.summary: The awakened spirits rise against the invaders, and Coral must choose sides mid-battle as friend and foe alike fall around him. Wren is gravely wounded shielding him. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: grief as clarity; neutrality dies, and only choice remains.

chapters.title: The Heart of the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: Coral reaches the heart-tree where the original curse was spoken, the fused prophecy's final line now legible: the speaker will lose what he loves most. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: terrible calm; he understands the price and prepares to pay it.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Voice
chapters.summary: At the heart-tree, Coral must speak the Wood's true name while holding love, not hatred, in mind — and the face he holds is Sera's, arrived bleeding at the treeline. POV: alternating Coral/Sera. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty.

chapters.title: The Speaking
chapters.summary: Coral speaks the name. The curse unbinds; the spirits wake free; the invading army falters as the Wood simply refuses war, disarming rather than destroying. Coral's swordspeech burns out of him. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: transcendence and loss entwined; victory that costs the victor himself.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Coral wakes remembering nothing of Wren, the Wood, or the past year — the price collected. Wren, freed, chooses exile over watching him forget her daily. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sorrow transfigured; freedom includes the freedom to grieve.

chapters.title: The Ledger Left Open
chapters.summary: Sera returns to the guild with Coral, who now keeps ordinary books. She tells him the story of everything he lost, refusing to let the truth die with his memory. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: tender persistence; love as the act of remembering aloud.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: One year later, Coral finds a new sapling growing through the guild floor — a cutting from the heart-tree, left by Wren — and feels something stir that is not memory but its echo. He plants it. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: quiet hope; some things, once given, find their way back.
